$comment: Composed from the bricks installed in this app. Apply with: node scripts/pb-schema.mjs <slug> pb/schema.json

collections.$comment: PocketBase ships `users` with createRule = "", i.e. ANYONE on the internet may register — and since every editorial collection grants full CRUD to `@request.auth.id != ""`, a stranger who signed up could list, edit and delete every brand, asset, post and variant of a public app. `create: null` makes account creation superuser-only: operators are created by the factory, never by self-signup. It is pinned here, declaratively, so a re-provision or a re-apply cannot quietly restore the default. `fields: []` is deliberate: pb-schema.mjs merges the desired fields over the live ones BY NAME, so an empty desired list preserves every built-in auth field (email, password, verified, tokenKey…) and changes nothing but the rules. `type: "auth"` is mandatory — pb-schema.mjs defaults to "base" and PocketBase would reject the PATCH. First in the list so `posts.approved_by` resolves on pass 1. `update`/`delete` are null for a reason found the hard way on 2026-08-14: PocketBase rules are per RECORD, not per field, so its default `id = @request.auth.id` ("you may edit yourself") lets an operator PATCH any field of their own row — including the `role` the auth brick adds. A member promoted themselves to admin with one request on a canary. Nothing legitimate is lost: the factory writes these rows through the DAO, which does not consult these rules.
collections.name: users
